clue.text: Moving sphere in evening sky

indicators.note: the letters of the word sphere are set in motion, so they are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A planet drifts across the sky at dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges SPHERE; the whole clue also describes the answer, the evening star, a planet (a moving sphere) seen in the evening sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The old poetic name for Venus as the evening star, a wandering planet shining after sunset.

clue.text: Gun with zero adjustment

indicators.note: adjustment means the letters are reset into a new order

explanation.surface: Zeroing in the sights of a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-barrelled artillery piece firing shells at a high angle.

clue.text: Work in army support is not on the level?

indicators.note: in places the work word inside the support word

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm, so it is an arm-y support
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Military logistics work that isn't quite on the level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'army' is read as arm-y: the support is for an arm, a SLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanting ground is not level, though the clue hints at dishonesty.

clue.text: Produces, in French, means of sex discrimination

parts.note: en is the French for in
genders are the categories by which sex is distinguished

explanation.surface: A French film-maker produces something on sexual prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: To engender is to cause or give rise to something.

clue.text: Jack appears to go astray with the drink

parts.note: a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, and an able seaman is abbreviated AB
to go astray morally is to sin
with is a link word bringing the next word in as written

explanation.surface: A sailor seems to wander off course and blames the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears' is just a link between Jack and the rest; the pieces AB, SIN and THE simply follow one another.
explanation.definitionFit: A green, wormwood-flavoured spirit, a strong liquor of nineteenth-century Paris.

clue.text: Where to buy cut-price computer for publican's profits

parts.note: a publican earns money at the bar, so bar gain
one who computes is a counter

explanation.surface: A computer bought with a landlord's takings.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are given in reverse clue order: the profits come first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop display of reduced goods, where discounted items are sold.

clue.text: Devil take the foreign press

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A demon seizes the foreign newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to urge or drive someone on.

clue.text: Water tortoise misses soft ground

indicators.note: misses means goes without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a terrapin is a freshwater turtle
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A turtle misses the soft ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land considered by its physical features.

clue.text: Blow-out said to land Henry in the river

indicators.note: in means the name is put inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
Hal is the familiar form of the name Henry, as Prince Hal

explanation.surface: A rumour that Henry was dumped in the river after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said to land' is the link: Henry, as he is called, lands in the river. THE EXE is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhale is to breathe out, a blowing out of air.

clue.text: Ne'er-do-well reformed gratis

parts.note: someone reformed has become good
gratis means free, without payment

explanation.surface: A layabout claims to have turned over a new leaf free of charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle, worthless person is a layabout or wastrel.

clue.text: Transgressor word negro misspelled

indicators.note: the two words are spelt wrongly, signalling their letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that an offensive word has been spelt wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A transgressor breaks a law or moral rule, a sinner or offender.

clue.text: Fish in a bird-cage?

definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish with spiny fins
the bar a caged bird sits on

explanation.surface: A fish somehow kept in a bird-cage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a spiny freshwater fish and a roost bar for a bird, two unrelated senses of one word.

clue.text: Matched like those pursuing the bull

definitions.meaning: paired up, made into an identical pair
in the zodiac Gemini, the Twins, follows Taurus, the Bull

explanation.surface: Paired up like the runners chasing a bull through the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: The bull is Taurus; the sign after it in the zodiac is Gemini, the Twins, so they pursue it round the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Paired as identical partners; also, made into the Twins, the zodiac sign following Taurus.

clue.text: Bad weather forecast by Macbeth's witches

definitions.text: Bad weather forecast by Macbeth's witches

parts.words: Bad weather forecast by Macbeth's witches
parts.note: read as a forecast of icy pellets everywhere, and as the greeting the three witches give Macbeth in the play

explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial greeting, the salutation of the witches in Shakespeare's play; read literally, a prediction of hailstones throughout.

clue.text: Big bird beats the small one of course

definitions.text: beats the small one of course
definitions.meaning: on a golf course a score two under par beats a birdie, one under par

explanation.surface: A large bird outdoes a small one on its flight path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small one' is a birdie in golf (one under par); the score that beats it is two under par.
explanation.definitionFit: A large raptor, and in golf a hole played two strokes under par, bettering a birdie.

clue.text: Not worried about right title for decoration

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the rest
worried here means shaken about, so the letters of not are jumbled

parts.note: a title is a name

explanation.surface: Someone unconcerned about the proper title for an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' jumbles NOT into ONT, and 'about' puts that around R plus NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental object or embellishment is a decoration.

clue.text: Retreat here for Cromwell's general?

parts.note: a religious retreat for monks, punning on George Monck, the general who served Cromwell

explanation.definitionFit: A religious house where monks live in seclusion, and General Monck's name suggests he belongs there.

clue.text: Name wrongly, so fail to become champion, say

indicators.note: say means the phrase is heard rather than written

parts.note: to fail to win a championship is to miss the title

explanation.surface: Calling the runner-up by the wrong name.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something an incorrect name or heading.

clue.text: One who took the lead in Belmont

definitions.text: One who took the lead in Belmont

parts.words: One who took the lead in Belmont
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice, the suitor at Portia's house in Belmont who chose the lead casket and won her

explanation.definitionFit: Portia's successful suitor in Shakespeare's comedy picked the casket made of lead.

clue.text: New time-ban for investing

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh restriction on putting money into shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' is used in its old sense of surrounding or enveloping, not putting money in.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrounding on all sides; to invest a place is to encircle it.

clue.text: Retiring she is one to lament

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to lament is to moan

explanation.surface: A shy woman who is always grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' turns I MOAN round. Naomi, in the Book of Ruth, lamented her losses and asked to be called Mara, bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, the mother-in-law of Ruth in the Bible.

clue.text: Exaggerate part beyond measure

parts.note: beyond means over
a measure passed by parliament is an act

explanation.surface: An actor going over the top in a role.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham up a role is to play it too broadly.

clue.text: Sounds like a stop order on a bank

indicators.note: sounds like means the word is heard, spelt differently

parts.note: to check is to halt, a stop

explanation.surface: Stopping a payment at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A written instruction telling a bank to pay money from an account.

clue.text: Practice at home

parts.note: a practice is a habit, a regular custom

explanation.surface: Doing one's practice at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The natural environment where an animal or plant lives is its home.

clue.text: The army's eighth star in the constellation

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A soldier's guide to the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth Greek letter, used to label a constellation's eighth brightest star.

clue.text: Beginning the North America trail

parts.note: NA is the abbreviation for North America
a scent is the trail an animal leaves

explanation.surface: The start of a journey across the American continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent things are just coming into being, emerging.

clue.text: File awaiting attention

definitions.meaning: a line of people one behind another
waiting one's turn to be served

explanation.surface: A document left in the in-tray.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of people waiting their turn: in single file, and waiting to be served.

clue.text: Nile agent disposed to be crude

indicators.note: disposed means arranged differently, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An agent on the Nile who is inclined to be rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking grace or refinement, clumsy and unpolished.

clue.text: Kitchener first set out to alienate

indicators.note: first says the jumbled word goes in front of the other piece
out means put out of order, so the letters of set are jumbled

parts.note: a kitchener is an old word for a kitchen range or stove

explanation.surface: Lord Kitchener sets out first to drive people away.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitchener is not the field marshal but a kitchen stove, a RANGE; 'out' jumbles SET into EST, which 'first' puts in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to make them hostile or distant, to turn them away.

clue.text: Try to split tree back in the shrubbery

indicators.note: back means the whole result is read in reverse
to split means to break into the tree word, so the other piece goes inside it

parts.note: an elm is a tree
taken as written

explanation.surface: Attempting to fell a tree at the back of the garden bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to split' puts TRY inside ELM to make ELTRYM, and 'back' reverses that whole run.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen bush with fragrant white flowers, the kind of plant found among the bushes.
